title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages). E and K are extensions of Q, possibly infinite algebraic. Spec(E⊗K) is the profinite set of pairs of embeddings (E→Qbar, K→Qbar) modulo the diagonal Galois action. A 'structure CM' Σ on the couple (E,K) is an open-closed subset (equivalently an idempotent ideal) of E⊗K. Its condition is that (τ×1)Σ = Σ' (the complement) for every complex conjugation τ. The previous page shows this is equivalent to (1×τ)Σ = Σ', so the notion is symmetric in E and K. It also shows that Σ is stable under extension of either field.

1. Minimal field of definition. There is a smallest couple (E0,K0), with E0⊂E and K0⊂K, such that Σ comes from an ideal of E0⊗K0. In modern terms:
- E0 is the CM field on which the CM type is primitive.
- K0 is the reflex field.
The symmetry of the formalism makes 'field of definition' and 'reflex field' the same notion seen from the two sides. Both are necessarily of CM type (the transcription's 'non vides' is probably 'non réels').

2. Degree bound. If [E0:Q] = 2d, then K0 is finite of degree ≤ C(2d,d). The reason is that Gal(Qbar/Q) acts on the d-element subsets of Hom(E0,Qbar), a set of 2d elements, and K0 is the fixed field of the stabiliser of the orbit.

3. Rank. If [E:Q] = 2d, then Λ(Σ) = (E⊗K)/Σ, the Σ-component, is free of rank d over K, and conversely.

4. CM bimodules. A bimodule t over (E,K), i.e. an E⊗K-module, is 'of CM type' if it is monogenic with CM annihilator. Up to isomorphism such modules correspond bijectively to CM structures Σ. Model case: the Lie algebra of a CM abelian variety as a module over E⊗(reflex field).

5. Reflex norm as a determinant. For K finite, t determines a homomorphism of Q-tori Ψ_Σ : T_K = R_{K/Q}G_m → T_E = R_{E/Q}G_m by Ψ_Σ(x) = det_{t/E}(x|t). Refined using the characteristic function 1_Σ of the clopen Σ, this is Ψ_Σ(x) = N_{E⊗K/E}(x^{1_Σ}), where x^{1_Σ} is x on the Σ-component and 1 elsewhere. This is exactly the reflex norm, defined intrinsically and symmetrically.

6. Functoriality. For K⊂K' and E⊂E' with pulled-back Σ', one has Ψ_{Σ'} = i_{E'/E} ∘ Ψ_Σ ∘ N_{K'/K}.

Next page. The reduction to the minimal couple; the cocharacter matrix of Ψ_Σ is 1_Σ on I_E×I_K; in the embedding description Ψ_Σ = σ1⋯σd; Ψ_Σ restricted to the totally real subfield is the norm. Hence Ψ_Σ kills the norm-one torus of K_r and factors through a Serre-type quotient torus S^K → T_E. The purpose of the whole passage is to set up CM motives and the Serre group / motivic Galois group of CM motives inside the 1965 'Galois theory of motives'.
errors: The bound [K0:Q] ≤ C(2d,d) is correct but not sharp. The Galois orbit consists of CM types, i.e. d-subsets containing exactly one element of each conjugate pair, and there are only 2^d of these. The standard bound is [K0:Q] ≤ 2^d, and C(2d,d) ≥ 2^d.

The text says 'un Σ' dans E⊗K'' but the diagram involves E' as well; Σ' should be the pullback to E'⊗K'. With that reading the commutativity claim is correct: the determinant over E' of x acting on (t⊗_E E')⊗_K K' equals det_{t/E}(N_{K'/K}x).

The formula det_{t/E} only makes sense for K finite (t finite over E); the parenthetical restricting to that case is somewhat garbled. For infinite K the clopen and characteristic-function formalism is needed, and the norm formula is then only meaningful after descending to a finite level.

ideas.what: Symmetric formulation of a CM type as a clopen subset (idempotent ideal) Σ of Spec(E⊗K), allowing infinite algebraic fields
ideas.modern_name: CM type as a function on Hom(E,Qbar)×Hom(K,Qbar), symmetric in a field and its reflex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama (reflex type); symmetric and Galois-set formulations in Deligne, Milne (1970s–80s)

ideas.what: Minimal couple (E0,K0) of definition of Σ: primitive CM field together with reflex field
ideas.modern_name: Primitive CM type and reflex field

ideas.what: Bound on the reflex field degree, [K0:Q] ≤ C(2d,d)
Bimodules of CM type: monogenic E⊗K-modules with CM annihilator, classified by Σ
ideas.modern_name: E⊗E*-module V_Φ (Lie algebra of a CM abelian variety)

ideas.what: Reflex norm defined as Ψ_Σ(x) = det_{t/E}(x) = N_{E⊗K/E}(x^{1_Σ}) as a morphism of Q-tori T_K → T_E, with functoriality in both fields
ideas.modern_name: Reflex norm N_{Φ*}: T_{E*} → T_E, a = det_E(a|V_Φ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama (as a product of embeddings); determinant/torus form in Deligne, Milne

missed.claim: As early as 1965, Grothendieck has the intrinsic, symmetric, torus-theoretic definition of the reflex norm as a determinant on a CM bimodule. He also has its functoriality in both fields and, on the next page, its factorisation through a Serre-type torus. This anticipates the formalism that later became standard through Serre (1968) and Deligne/Milne in the 1970s–80s. The novelty is priority and formulation, not mathematical content.
missed.quote: Un tel t définit un homom. Ψ_Σ : T_K → T_E ... Ψ_Σ(x) = dét_{t/E}(x_t) ... Ψ_Σ(x) = N_{E⊗K/E}(x^{1_Σ})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that the CM part of the motivic Galois group (Serre group, reflex norms as morphisms of tori) was being built into Grothendieck's motivic Galois theory in 1965. The CM-motive/Serre-group picture is now mostly credited to Serre and Deligne.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard CM theory: reflex field, reflex norm, degree bound. The 1965 determinant/bimodule definition of the reflex norm as a torus morphism, set in a symmetric profinite formalism and embedded in a motivic Galois programme, is early and not credited to Grothendieck. However, the mathematics itself is well known.
transcription_corrections: 'On a vu que E0, K0 sont nécessairement non vides' is probably 'non réels' (i.e. CM), consistent with the next page.
'(si E K fini sur Q, i.e. t fini sur E)' should read '(si K fini sur Q, i.e. t fini sur E)'; E with a struck-through or overwritten letter.

'des tores (sur Q) ... sur les Q-vectoriels sur Q (pour fixer les idées)' is garbled duplication. Probable reading: 'des tores (sur Q) (groupes multiplicatifs ...) dont l'action sur les points rationnels sur Q (pour fixer les idées) est donnée par'.
'et Ē cal. de E' is probably 'et Ē clôture algébrique de E' (or 'galoisienne').
'un Σ' dans E⊗K'' should likely be 'E'⊗K'' given the diagram.
